desc: In c-engine/Engine.cpp engineStart(), add env-gated frame-time recording: if ENGINE_FRAME_TIMES_LOG is set, each frame after timerEnd() push {timeSinceStartSeconds, timer.frameTime, timer.elapsed} into a std::vector (reserve ~8192). Per-frame cost must be just push_backs — no file I/O, no logging, no allocation-heavy work.
result: Recorder implemented in engineStart(): 24-byte FrameTimeSample, reserved vector, single push_back after timerEnd(); clean ninja build, 6 s play run exited cleanly with recorder active.

desc: After the main loop exits in engineStart(), do a single blocking write of all recorded samples to the path from ENGINE_FRAME_TIMES_LOG: one header line, then 'time_offset_s frame_time_ms cpu_work_ms' per line, plus a summary block (count, mean, stdev, p50, p95, p99, max for both the frameTime and elapsed series). Log the path and summary via utils::info; handle write failure gracefully (log error, don't crash). Keep the vector and write inside engineStart() (local storage, after the loop).

Run a ~25 s capture: ENGINE_FRAME_TIMES_LOG=/tmp/frame_times.txt ENGINE_HITCH_DEBUG=1 ./scripts/run.sh play log 25000. Confirm the game reaches gameplay, exits at the log timeout, and /tmp/frame_times.txt has a sane line count (~1500+); also note whether game.log contains HITCH lines (zero HITCH lines while MangoHud flickers is itself a finding). Fix any crash/warning if found (gdb with ENGINE_DEBUG=1 if it crashes). Do not touch the parked player/camera rows in db.db.

Analyze /tmp/frame_times.txt with a small Python one-off: percentiles/stdev for both the frameTime and cpuWork series, histogram buckets, spike frames (>2x p50) with time offsets, and periodicity check (spike every Nth frame / fixed period). Join spike time offsets against game.log wall-clock events (terrain tile streaming, futureTask, loading, HITCH lines) to form a suspect list (terrain streaming, GPU vsync latency, GC-like pauses). If 1-second timeSinceStartSeconds granularity proves too coarse for the join, first swap the field to timer.timeSinceStart / BILLION (double, same 24 bytes) and re-record.

Write findings to .miniagent/ledger/notes.md: quantified instability (baseline frame time, spike magnitude/frequency/periodicity), likely suspect subsystems, and recommended next steps. This is the deliverable answering task.md's 'frame times are not stable' question.
